events.text: The Battle of the Evermoors was a conflict fought sometime around 1400 DR between Uthgardt warriors of the Elk tribe and a cell of the Cult of the Dragon and the black dragon Rakor for control of the helmet of disjunction.
The Alliance of Freesailors between Cormyr, Sembia and Impiltur was disbanded, allowing Cormyr to refocus its navy on its nation instead of on opposing piracy.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: The island of Snowdown came under the control of Amn. This annexation happened after a slow but steady consolidation of power on the island as well as a civil war against the Kendrick Dynasty believed to have been supported by Amn.
In the Year of the Sceptered One, 1404 DR, Amn hired mercenaries to invade Snowdown.
Emvar Obarskyr was born to Azoun V and Queen Nalara.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Entry to the Haunted Halls of Eveningstar was forbidden without an explicit warrant from the Crown after a dozen adventuring companies were wiped out.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: High Queen Alicia Kendrick died unexpectedly. It was commonly believed that she was poisoned by agents of Lionel Carrathal, the heir to the former Carrathal Dynasty who claimed to be the "true" High King. The Callidyrr dragoons quelled subsequent unrest.
cites: Dragon 405: Heroes of the Moonshaes, с. 5

events.text: Urmlaspyr was annexed into Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Foril Obarskyr was born to Azoun V and Queen Nalara.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: After an epidemic decimated the population of metallic dragons in the Copper Mountains, many of them evacuated the region. One such dragon, Skalnaedyr, fled south to the village of Phannaskull and offered protection for their obedience. He became the first of many Dragon princes to claim power in the greater region of Murghôm.

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: The town of Phannaskull later changed its name to Skalnaedyr, after its draconic prince. The more moderate members of the Cult established the Dragon House within the city, while its fringe members operated out of the nearby Tower of the Talon.

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: In the Year of True Omens the Copper Mountains were ravaged by a draconic plague that infected metallic dragons.

Following years of steady expansion by the fey of Sarifal into the territory of Corwell, conflict with Amnian mercenaries resulted in Corwell being put to the torch, which prompted High Lady Ordalf to expel the remaining humans from the isle.
By the year of 1412 DR the entire region fell under full control of the Dragon Princes of Murghôm.
Loyal members of House Cormaeril were restored to nobility by Azoun V, but their lands were kept by the Crown.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18
Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 6

events.text: After decades of increased financial influence and foreign investment, Sembian administrators bloodlessly took over leadership of Featherdale.
Tasseldale was overrun by mercenaries from Yhaunn.
Elversult became a protectorate of the realm.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Battledale restricted trade with and travel to Sembia after their seizure of Featherdale. The nation responded with a heavy assault, which led to the evacuation of the city of Essembra.
In an effort to stave of Sembian encroachment, High Dale officially seceded from the Dales Council and became a settlement of Cormyr.
In 1424 DR they declared their independence from the Tethyr and became an autonomous duchy.
Ashabenford, then the permanent seat of the Dales Council, reaffirmed the Dales Compact with Myth Drannor and restored the Standing Stone.
Teziir joined Cormyr, completing the country's control of the lands and ports around the Dragonmere. Westgate, under the control of House Bleth, is a notable exception.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: The Seven Burghers of Harrowdale formed an official allaince with restored Myth Drannor. This resulted in the renaming of Harrowdale Town to New Velar.
Marriage of Foril Obarskyr to Jemra Rhindaun, niece to Queen Sybille of Tethyr, to the displeasure of the nobility.
Irvel Obarskyr was born to Prince Foril and Princess Jemra.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Crown Prince Emvar was assassinated in an ambush by Sembian forces, south of the Vast Swamp. Within a month, Princess Jemra was also killed during a failed Sembian assassination attempt of King Azoun V. The public mourned and called for action against Netheril and Sembia.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Royal Magician Ganrahast discovered Emvar's illegitimate son Erzoured and his mother Solatha, a merchant's daughter. Ganrahast brought them to the palace and where Solatha was ennobled as Countess of Dhedluk, her birthplace.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Tensions with Sembia escalated into open war.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: The Swords of Archendale were unmasked after it was discovered they had been bought out by Sembia, allowing the dale to avoid Sembian annexation.
Branwyn Moonsinger, the granddaughter to the late High Queen Alicia Kendrick, was made Great Druid of Sarifal.

The war ended with a peace treaty drafted between Netherese Sembia, Cormyr, Cormanthor and the Dalelands. The Treaty of Griffonfang Bridge re-declared the independence of the cities of Daerlun and Urmlaspyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: The war effectively ended the Huntsilver noble family and the marriages of the two surviving daughters into the Houses of Crownsilver and Truesilver.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Azoun V restored the Goldfeather family to nobility.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Foril Obarskyr carried the ensign of the Purple Dragon into battle.
Prince Irvel married Ospra Goldfeather.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Death of King Azoun V. Coronation of King Foril.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: King Foril officially recognised Erzoured as Emvar Obarskyr's son, having secured his own legacy.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 9

events.text: During 1451 DR, Netherese loyalists led by Herzgo Alegni infiltrated the power structure of Neverwinter, trying to take advantage of the situation of the city to locate old Xinlenal.
In the summer of 1451 DR, a small adventuring party rediscovered ancient Gauntlgrym beneath the nearby Mount Hotenow, and as part of a Red Wizard plot, briefly awoke the primordial Maegera.

The Ruining, also known as the Cataclysm or simply the eruption of Mount Hotenow, was the destruction of the city of Neverwinter when Mount Hotenow erupted at the end of the summer of the Year of Knowledge Unearthed, 1451 DR.
An extended war between the Shadovar and Thay was fought over the city of Neverwinter in the mid-to-late 15th century DR.
Baerovus Obarskyr was born to Crown Prince Irvel and Princess Ospra.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: In the Year of the Mithral Hammer, 1456 DR, Cvaal's son Talaric Daoran decided to send loggers into the Quivering Forest, voiding his father's agreement with the fey; Talaric mysteriously disappeared that night, never to be seen again, and was succeeded by his son Anivar.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 81

events.text: In 1459 DR, following political unrest caused by the assassination of Gareth's descendant, Queen Brianne Dragonsbane, the Warlock Knights marshaled an army of conscripts and evil humanoids to rebel against the Kingdom of Bloodstone.
Circa the Year of the Forged Sigil, 1459 DR, Elturgard learned that shrines to unapproved primal entities existed in the Reaching Woods.
Raedra Obarskyr was born to Crown Prince Irvel and Princess Ospra.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: In 1463 DR, Menzoberranyr drow talking about the city said it had never been rebuilt.

In the Year of the Reborn Hero, 1463 DR, Thayans and their Ashmadai allies attacked Neverwinter, hoping to cause enough deaths to fuel a Dread Ring, but their plans were foiled with the help of adventurers and some Netherese agents.

In the Year of the First Circle, 1468 DR, Open Lord Dagult Neverember of Waterdeep, seeing an opportunity to add to his financial empire, proclaimed to be a descendant of Neverwinter's former rulers and thus the rightful "Lord Protector" of the city, starting the New Neverwinter movement.

In the Year of the First Circle, 1468 DR, Lord Dagult Neverember, seeing an opportunity to add to his financial empire, hired workers to help rebuild the city and Mintarn mercenaries to protect it from monsters and bandits.
In 1469 DR, Queen Cyndra died and was succeeded by her daughter, Queen Arathane.
In 1469 DR, a group of oni appeared in Fimbrul and organized the usually scattered Fimbran orc tribes into formidable war bands.
The traditionally thief-ruled city of Proskur was declared a protectorate of Cormyr, supposedly to protect it from Netheril.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: King Foril sealed the city of Wheloon, converting it into a prison colony in response to unprecedented Shar faithful activity and evidence of an alliance with Netheril.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: By the Year of the Fourth Circle, 1474 DR, the Sons of Alagondar emerged as an insurgent group that opposed the rule of Lord Neverember.
Circa 1474 DR, Jarant killed the previous King of Snakes Ebarnaje, triggering a civil war and increasing yuan-ti and lizardfolk activity in the area.
In the Year of the Fifth Circle, 1476 DR, the entire garrison of paladins at Fort Morninglord disappeared overnight and every stone in the fort was blackened and every door and window fused shut.
In the Year of the Purloined Statue, 1477 DR tensions between the Fire Knives and the Nine Golden Swords reached a breaking point and gang warfare erupted across Westgate.
In the Year of the Purloined Statue, 1477 DR, a large earthquake struck Vaasa, causing the ruins of Castle Perilous to rejuvenate mysteriously into an imposing dark fortress.
In the Year of the Dark Circle, 1478 DR, the Harpers cell in Neverwinter suffered a devastating blow.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, Ashanath remained largely unsettled.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, Baldur's Gate was Faerûn's most powerful and important city, and it was once again stable.
The Battle of Lendon's Dike was a battle in the Moonsea region between the defenders of Hulburg and their mercenaries against the Warlock Knights and their orc and hobgoblin allies.
The Battle of Luthcheq was a conflict between the nations of Chessenta, Akanûl, and Tymanther against the dragon players of Brimstone's xorvintaal that took place in the Year of the Ageless One.
The Battle of the Fortress of the Half-Demon was fought in late 1479 DR between undead Durthans and their humanoid allies and Rashemi berserkers and fey commanded by Aoth Fezim.

links.t: Battle of the Fortress of the Half-Demon

src.title: Battle of the Fortress of the Half-Demon

events.text: By 1479 DR, Berdusk had been incorporated into the young theocratic realm of Elturgard.

In 1479 DR, his descendant, Shala Karanok, was the ruler of Chessenta when Tchazzar was rescued from the Shadowfell by the Brotherhood of the Griffon, as part of the plans of the dragon player's of Brimstone's xorvintaal, and became ruler of Chessenta once again.
The Council of the Dragon was a noble moot called by King Foril Obarskyr I of Cormyr to discuss the ruling of the Realm.

By 1479 DR, King Frostmantle's reign was characterized by increased threats to Damara's borders, including monsters from the Great Glacier and Frostfell to the north (such as the mysterious "Breath of Winter"), demons from the Dunwood to the east, and raiders from Narfell to the northeast.
By 1479 DR, the vampires and bandits of Erlkazar still raided Amn, Calimshan, Tethyr, and Turmish and their lair, to those that knew about it, was called the Night Barony.

In the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, the Storm Maiden of Norland sought to rally the Northlanders to purge the giants from the island, and had successfully forayed into the South Jotunhammer Mountains and slain some Grondsgrunn patrols to prove her ability to lead such a conquest.
In 1479 DR, the blue dragon Gestaniius used an army of dragonspawn, purple worms and other minions to try to conquer High Imaskar, as part of her plot to gain more points in Brimstone's xorvintaal.
By 1479 DR, the Field Ward had been established and Skullport was no longer inhabited.

In 1479 DR these ruins sat at the southern end of a lake that was no longer connected to the Lake of Steam, and this smaller lake itself was just directly south of the Plaguewrought Land. The Lake of Steam was restored to its previous area following the events of the Second Sundering.
The Invasion of Tymanther was a conflict between the nation of Tymanther and the forces of the green dragon Skuthosiin that took place in the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR.

In the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, a band of Auril-worshiping frost giants were called to these ruins by a Zhengyian artifact, and slew a band of Banite Warlock Knights who were likewise seeking this artifact.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, after Alustriel's apparent demise, her eldest son, Methrammar Aerasumé, was High Lord of Luruar.
By 1479 DR Maerimydra was firmly under the control of the fire giants, led by the fire titan, Queen Hledh Hellspawn, Graz'zt's granddaughter.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, Bloodscar was effectively in open rebellion against Many-Arrows and was at war with the Neverwinter Guard.
In 1479 DR, the Dernall Forest of Alaron in the Moonshae Isles was invaded by inhabitants of Nachtur.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, Nathlan was a strong and independent nation sometimes known as "the Eastern nation of the West".
By 1479 DR, not a single ship encountered the island in almost a century.
By 1479 DR, the city of Olleth was under the total dominion of the Abolethic Sovereignty.
By 1479 DR, Secomber had become a place under constant threat of hobgoblin raids.

The Siege of Helm's Hold was a prolonged assault upon the city by its allied force that comprised its outcast leaders, soldiers of the Neverwinter Guard, along with some local allies and conscripted adventurers.
The Siege of Neverwinter was a conflict between the forces of Neverwinter and the Thayan forces under Valindra Shadowmantle that took place in the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR.
In 1479 DR, Gauwervyndhal empowered a few of her human and dragonborn slaves and sent them as envoys to the free lands of Laerakond, in hopes to create commercial treaties with those nations.
By 1479 DR, the island was larger in area than it was before the Spellplague.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition: Map

events.text: In the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, the resurrected Tchazzar rallied his army to defeat Alasklerbanbastos, subjugating Threskel as a vassal state of Chessenta.
Around 1479 DR, Tymanther was making a name for itself with its small elite cadres of soldiers attacking well-known dragon lairs.
In the Year of the Ageless Ones, 1479 DR, due to the plans of the taaldaraxi of Brimstone's xorvintaal, Tymanther was facing diplomatic problems with Chessenta and Akanûl.
Around 1479 DR, Ulgarth, Durpar, and Estagund were grouped under the northern Faerûn's appellation, the Beastlands.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, Norland had seceded and Norheim was likewise no longer under Kendrick rule.
By the Year of the Ageless One, 1479 DR, the Warlock Knights had turned an expansionist eye toward their neighbors, all of whom viewed the Knights as among the greatest threats in Faerûn.
